design_decisions.question: Does `unsafe` warrant its own `ControlFlowBlockKind` variant, the way `LetElseDiverge` did?
design_decisions.decision: No -- reuse `ControlFlowBlockKind::NestedBlockExpr`, the same kind a bare `{ .. }` block already uses. `LetElseDiverge` was justified as a new variant because reusing `IfElse` would conflate two GENUINELY DIFFERENT syntactic origins with different branch semantics (a pattern-match failure arm vs. an if's else arm). `unsafe` has no analogous distinction: it changes what operations are PERMITTED inside the block, not the block's control-flow SHAPE -- structurally it is exactly a nested block expression, confirmed by every other walker already treating it identically to `Expr::Block` for their own purposes. Adding a dedicated kind here would be exactly the premature enum proliferation this session's engineering-quality principles argue against.

design_decisions.question: How to share code between the `Expr::Block` and `Expr::Unsafe` arms in `lower_divergent` without duplicating the block-lowering logic?
design_decisions.decision: Combined them into one match arm (`syn::Expr::Block(_) | syn::Expr::Unsafe(_)`), extracting just the `&syn::Block` reference via a small inner match (`block_expr.block` vs. `unsafe_expr.block`) before the shared lowering logic runs once. Avoids a third near-duplicate copy of the reserve/lower_stmts/Branch-edge pattern.
